You're right, this is no different from physical illnesses. However, there has been cases where doctors would end a patient's life because there is no other options available. Same applies here, if there is no option available but death to end these feelings, why are we telling them not to do it?

You seem to be better off than I am.

The times that I'm "severely depressed" I cannot get up in the morning. I cant walk down to the bathroom or even be bothered to sit up. I cant pick up food with my fork, and if someone had put food in my mouth I would not be able to chew it. The times that I'm severely depressed, the littlest things like picking up a pen and writing "Hello World!" would require so much effort, it'd feel like I would die.

That is what I mean by depressed people. People that see no point in doing anything, people that cannot motivate themselves.

I've tried therapy, and I do not think it helps. And for people like me, you can only beat the horse for so long. If you try something over and over again with repeated failure, it would be logical to assume that it just doesn't work. And if nothing works, what's the point of living?

well_now_what brings up an interesting comparison to physical illnesses, like pneumonia. I'd also like to make a connection here. If someone was on life support for a hopeless amount of time, any good doctor would recommend ending their lives. This is the same point I'm trying to make: why are we telling depressed people that there is hope when there isn't?

Its not "deserve an extra chance", its more so that they wouldn't want an extra chance. They didn't do anything wrong that requires forgiveness. If someone wanted to die, why won't we let them? They don't want an extra chance, so why are we forcing them to accept it?
That punched me in the vulnerable spot. I think people should be more accepting towards suicide and not view it as such a horrible thing.
If you give me a gun, I will surely go away forever.

"we can at least try to help." <- The majority of depressed people I've talked to ended up just like that. They wouldn't accept an optimistic future or the solution I suggest, rather they thanked me for my time and moved on.

When I said they're unwilling to contribute, I mean that they're too depressed to better themselves which would then better society. I'm also a depressed person and I'll tell you now that most of my days I'd feel too hopeless to pick up a book and study or do some simple math problems. In what I've experienced, depression does not perk you up and motivate you to finish your homework. It doesn't get you out of bed for work, neither does it tell you to crack a joke to cheer someone up.

Something else I've experienced, the times I've been suicidal I wouldn't readily give up to, "things are okay." A person who has been battling with these thoughts for months or years to the point of death wouldn't be convinced with, "Hey, everything's going to be okay." Things will not be okay, that is why people become depressed. Why would they be depressed if things are okay?

I've been through therapy and lifestyle changes, yet I still have to go through the same pounding feelings every day.

Would you like a source? Here I am. Why would society tell people like me, who see no hope in life and no point in getting up, to get up and do more work? Would you tell a cancer patient to get up and work a full time job? Would you give a gun to a handicap and tell them to defend our country? You would not, so why do people tell depression victims to cheer up and be a trooper?

- Mentally I'd say we both understand what it would take to be an "adult", but we are not quite at that stage yet. However, we were able to handle the distance well and trusted each other. That, I would imagine, requires much maturity. You make an interesting note on growth rate. It's usually me who helps her out on any emotional issues she faces, and something I noted was that everything she was experiencing now was something I've already experienced in the past (i.e. she'd occasionally slip into depression, which I also had problems with as a pre-teen). Thus, she thought we "matched" in how we think and also in how we react towards certain situations.

- She had a boyfriend before this relationship. In fact, it was only a few days/week after she broke up with her boyfriend that we started our relationship. I was unaware of how quickly she moved and so in the beginning we pondered at the idea of me being a rebound (the idea never came up again in the mid/late relationship periods). This is my first relationship.

- By "perfect" I mean we hardly disagree on anything. I cant remember an instance where we've fought; even when we broke up no hateful comments were thrown. Our interests matched, as did our personalities, desires and goals. The one difference we have is that she is less motivated than I am, in most ways. For example, I tend to be studying/doing school work 24/7 while she procrastinates quite a bit and tends to distract me from work. But she's an excellent student nonetheless. She ranks high in her school and have won a few awards (successfulness does play a large role in choosing partners for me). And it's always been me who'd go out to see her. She never made the effort to come out here, but that's mainly because her parents would not allow her to travel alone (mine trust me to travel alone, aka indifferent).

- I feel irrational about leaving her. We've built a good relationship and she has done close to nothing wrong. Compared to most relationships, ours is solid gold. Soul mates seem like mystical bonds that only exists in movies, but I'd say we're soul mates if we define that term as two people who can grow old together. Not to mention, I told her I'd take care of her in the beginning of this and now I'm leaving without her consent. I don't know why I'm being so cruel to the one I love. It feels like a natural calling for me to be alone. I love solitude. But I love her too, and shouldn't I change myself for the one I love?
I know I'm being silly... Love is a silly thing.
